legend: This 55-year-old man presented with symptoms of a non-functioning sellar tumour, and his preoperative neuroimaging studies were thought to indicate non-functioning PitNET/adenoma on the basis of the presence of a homogeneous, well-demarcated sellar/suprasellar mass, as seen here; biopsy, however, proved this to be a pituicytoma.
The tumour cells are cytologically bland, with oval nuclei, minimal hyperchromatism, and eosinophilic cytoplasm.

Diffuse nuclear immunoreactivity for thyroid transcription factor 1 (TTF1) is typical of pituicytoma and confidently distinguishes it from schwannoma, meningioma, or pituitary adenoma, all of which are immunonegative.

diagnosis: Granular cell tumour of the sellar region / granular cell pituicytoma

legend: Tumour cells generally show more oval nuclei than those seen in schwannoma, which usually contains tapering nuclei with pointed ends. Note the absence of nuclear pseudoinclusions, which are seen in some meningioma cells. Note also the uniformity of nuclear features and absence of mitotic activity.
Intersecting fascicles of tumour cells show the plump eosinophilic cytoplasm typical of this tumour; increased cytoplasmic volume is due to increased mitochondrial content.

These tumours show diffuse nuclear immunoreactivity for thyroid transcription factor 1 (TTF1), but so do pituicytomas, granular cell tumours of the posterior pituitary, and even normal posterior pituitary gland, so this immunostain does not distinguish between these lesions.

legend: These sellar/suprasellar tumours are composed of small groups of cytologically bland spindle cells that usually show strong diffuse cytoplasmic immunoreactivity for S100.
Spindle cell oncocytomas show immunoreactivity for galectin-3, as seen here, as well as vimentin, S100, and antimitochondrial antibody.

Accumulation of mitochondria that often appear abnormal is the hallmark of spindle cell oncocytoma at ultrastructural examination. No secretory granules are present. A small extracellular lumen filled with microvilli (asterisk) is present. (Scale bar: 2 µm.)
This pituicytic tumour shows perivascular pseudorosettes similar to those seen in ependymomas of the CNS.
